fresh_internal_checks.check: The new unit declares connected compact X, dimension at least one, a Hermitian background and fixed Gauduchon forms on a set of smooth modifications.
The modification collection contains the identity and a common log resolution for each pair of analytic types; no countable reduction is asserted.
The smooth pulled-back Hermitian form is semipositive and positive on the nonempty isomorphism locus, giving a finite strictly positive denominator.
Modification descent gives a genuine pullback potential and a positive curvature current.
Distributional Stokes pairs the locally integrable pullback with a smooth Gauduchon test; closedness of the background is not required.
The total linear trace mass is the fixed denominator; this is not a bound on nonlinear top-degree mass.
Coefficientwise polar restriction and smooth positive wedging yield a positive measure of mass at most that denominator.
Total variation of two positive measures with those mass bounds is at most twice the denominator.
Each normalized coordinate is a pseudometric on genuine potentials, and symmetry and the triangle inequality persist under the supremum.
The supremum is bounded regardless of the cardinality of the fixed collection or a lack of a uniform positive lower bound for its denominators.
Scalar rescaling of a Gauduchon form multiplies numerator and denominator by the same positive power; independence of arbitrary metric shapes is not claimed.
A common analytic resolution has finitely many resolved prime components and bounded remainders; their positive coefficients determine the pole sets.
The existing local closed correction and divisorial restriction argument gives exactly the resolved coefficient times each integration current.
Different resolved components have no overlapping trace mass at intersections, and each has positive Hermitian trace mass.
Zero comparison forces equality of the measures on the chosen resolution and hence equality of all resolved coefficients.
The existing finite divisorial dominance criterion applies in both directions, giving bounded ordinary equivalence.
Ordinary projection is constant on that equivalence class, so normalized analytic ordinary models are equal.
Every smooth modification of a compact smooth curve is an isomorphism, with trace exponent zero and unchanged area.
Total variation is preserved by this curve pullback; the comparison is the existing complete polar metric divided by positive fixed area.
The curve completeness and analytic-closure assertions retain the full ordinary curve domain, including zero non-pluripolar mass.
A smooth gauge leaves the raw pulled-back curvature current and pole set unchanged, and Stokes leaves the same denominator.

The gauge assertion is explicitly before ordinary projection; the transformed background need not itself be Hermitian, because its denominators stay equal and its transported potentials remain admissible.
Ambient measure coordinates form a metric bounded by two and have coordinatewise Banach limits retaining positivity and mass bounds.
The Cauchy tail is uniform in all coordinates; passing to the limit separately and then taking the supremum proves ambient completeness.
The coordinate map preserves the pseudometric but is not called an embedding on every ordinary model.
Realization, general separation, full analytic closure, agreement with the positive-volume topology and background degeneration remain unproved; no general question is closed.
